messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
जब मैंने उसे महान रेगिस्तान में देखा, मैंने उससे कहा “मुझ पर दया करो” और चिल्लाया, तुम चाहे जो भी हो चाहे छाया हो या निश्चित रूप से मनुष्य!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Quando | temporal conjunction “at the time that” | जब | “when” | OK | | vidi | past perception “saw” | देखा | “saw” | OK | | costui | demonstrative pronoun “him” | उसे | “him” | OK | | nel | preposition “in” | में | “in” | OK | | gran | adjective “great” | महान | “great” | OK | | diserto | noun “desert” | रेगिस्तान | “desert” | OK | | Miserere | imperative “have pity” | दया करो | “have pity” | OK | | di | preposition “on” | पर | “on” | OK | | me | pronoun “me” | मुझ | “me” | OK | | gridai | past verb “cried / shouted” | चिल्लाया | “shouted” | OK | | a | preposition “to” | (part of) उससे | “to” (embedded) | OK | | lui | pronoun “him” | उससे | “him” (as object of “to”) | OK | | qual | relative pronoun “whatever” | जो | “whatever/that which” | OK | | che | relative particle (connects *qual* with clause) | — | (none) | UNNECESSARY | | tu | pronoun “you” | तुम | “you” | OK | | sii | subjunctive verb “be” | हो | “be” | OK | | od | conjunction “or” (first) | चाहे | “or” (first) | OK | | ombra | noun “shade” | छाया | “shade” | OK | | od | conjunction “or” (second) | या | “or” (second) | OK | | omo | noun “man” | मनुष्य | “man” | OK | | certo | adjective “certain / real” | निश्चित रूप से | “certainly / for sure” | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *che* – the relative particle has no direct counterpart in Hindi and is omitted without loss of meaning. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected; all target words convey the intended meanings and agree in gender/number where applicable.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 1: - Original: जब मैंने उसे महान रेगिस्तान में देखा, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 2: - Original: मैंने उससे कहा “मुझ पर दया करो” और चिल्लाया, - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 3: - Original: तुम चाहे जो भी हो चाहे छाया हो या निश्चित रूप से मनुष्य! - Issue: GRAMMAR (redundant “चाहे”) - Corrected: तुम चाहे जो भी हो, छाया हो या निश्चित रूप से मनुष्य!
